newsitem.title: CHILE: Banco Edwards studies bond issue - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Banco Edwards studies bond issue - CEO.

text.p: Chile's Banco de A. Edwards is studying issuing subordinated bonds in international markets for $50 million to $100 million in the second half of the year, said general manager Gustavo Favre.
"We are studying the possibility that the bank issues bonds for an important amount...$50 million to $100 million or the equivalent," Favre told Reuters in an interview.
"We are looking to see whether the issue, or part of it, could be issued abroad."
A final decision should be made by the end of June but the bank has not ruled out a much smaller placement of around $20 million in the Santiago market, said Favre.
"Let's hope we can clear up all the points within 40 days from now. The operation will be in the second half of the year, whatever happens," he said.

The decision whether to go locally or abroad will depend on whether Central Bank rules on the use of funds from bond issues allow the bank to invest the proceeds as it plans, he said. If Edwards decided to go abroad, it would not be economic to make a placement for under $50 million, said Favre.
The fact the bank already trades in New York should make it easier to get approval for the placement from U.S. regulatory authorities, he said.

The bank, the fourth largest private bank in Chile in terms of its loan portfolio, will use funds from the operation to finance future growth and ensure that its capital base remains within the international Basel standards.
Edwards, which started trading on Wall Street in 1995, issued $24 million of subordinated bonds locally last year.
The bank's plans include moving into Argentina and Peru to offer financial services to Chilean clients who have investments abroad, said Favre.
"We are studying Argentina, especially Buenos Aires, to see what would be the best way to begin business there," he said.
Any investment would be small and may include opening a representation office, but the company has ruled out buying a foreign bank, he said.
The bank should make a decision on moves abroad by the end of the year, said Favre.
Edwards expects its loan portfolio to grow by 15 percent in real terms this year -- higher than the 10 percent growth expected for Chile's banking sector, he said.
The bank, which has a $3.5 billion loan portfolio, concentrates on offering services to high-income individuals and to small and medium-sized companies.
Edwards reported net income of 5.4 billion pesos in the first three months of the year, up from five billion pesos in the same period of 1996.
